doc.title: Slide Hampton interviewed by Monk Rowe, West Orange, New Jersey, July 30, 2003

title: Money and the Indianapolis learning community
summary: Economic problems were self-made; as youths they practiced all day at Attucks High School and traded knowledge.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Has there been a time, from an economic standpoint, that’s been toughest in your career, a period of years?

Not really. I find that all the things about economics and all of that that’s a problem for me, are problems that I made myself. It wasn’t what was happening in society or in general. It was whenever I had a problem with those things I made that problem myself. And when we were coming up we were so interested in learning we never thought about money. You know we were practicing all day man. People were sick of us. They’d say you guys are crazy, you’re never going to do anything, you’re spending all this time playing all this funny music. And we loved it so much we never were offended, we never though about oh we’re going to make money or we’re not going to make money. We never thought about that. All we thought about, man how can we learn to play a C seven, how many different ways can we play a C seven? That’s what we were doing every day, from the morning to night.
This is the group in Indianapolis. Were you in the same school? Freddie Hubbard and those guys?
My brothers and sisters were. Yeah they were all in Attucks High School.
Okay. But it was just a congregation of people that had that same passion.

Yeah there were a lot of musicians there — there were classical musicians and the jazz musicians were studying together. They were actually trading experience and knowledge with each other. And we’d get together and play, we’d get together and read music just for the fun of it, and we’d get together and try to write an arrangement and have somebody to play it. It was horrible, but we were so glad to have the opportunity to try. That was that thing that we thought about.
Yeah. To get to hear those things, and experiment, and find out what works and what doesn’t.
It was wonderful. It was wonderful just to think that it might sound like something. And often it didn’t. But we enjoyed the part before we heard that.
